obligations.title: Accommodate and protect the complete driver population
obligations.statement: Accommodate the 5th-percentile female through 95th-percentile male population in seating, controls and driver equipment. Keep the driver's head and hands clear of the ground in every rollover orientation. Event-site anthropometry is an external input that has not yet been selected.
conditions_and_alternatives: All team drivers and the prescribed anthropometric range; no single nominal driver is substituted.
obligations.verification_obligation: Review an approved anthropometric dataset and every driver/equipment combination. Check reach and occupant geometry and sweep all rollover orientations, including restrained head and hand envelopes.
unresolved_decisions: Driver dataset, team driver measurements, equipment and adjustable seating/control geometry TBD.

obligations.title: Choose and substantiate the primary structure
obligations.statement: The primary structure may use steel tubing/material, an allowed alternative tubing material, composite material or a combination. A mixed tube-frame/monocoque/tube/composite design must satisfy the relevant material rules, applicable structural equivalence and connection requirements. No construction is selected by this candidate model.
conditions_and_alternatives: Tube, monocoque and hybrid alternatives remain unresolved.

The source F.5.1.1 and F.3.2.1 references to F.3.4.4 are retained as published; F.3.5 actually contains the aluminum provisions. Seek official clarification rather than silently changing the reference.
obligations.verification_obligation: Select construction in the structural equivalence submission; enumerate every material and transition joint and substantiate equivalence, fastening, bonding and monocoque attachments under the applicable referenced clauses.
unresolved_decisions: Chassis type, material grades, laminates, connections and equivalence evidence TBD.

obligations.title: Apply tubing classes and material restrictions
obligations.statement: Assign steel tube classes by application: A for front hoop, main hoop and shoulder-harness mounting bar; B for front bulkhead, front-hoop bracing, side-impact structure, main-hoop bracing, harness attachment and battery mounting/protection; C for front-bulkhead supports, main-hoop brace supports, shoulder-bar bracing, component protection and structural tubing; D for bent upper side-impact members. Aluminum is prohibited for the main hoop, main-hoop bracing and shoulder-harness mounting bar; it is permitted conditionally for the other listed applications. Tubing below the structural class is nonstructural and cannot be credited for rule compliance.
conditions_and_alternatives: All rows of the application table are preserved as constraints, including battery protection which is only an interface to this slice.
obligations.verification_obligation: Build a member/application/material matrix, confirm each required class and prohibited aluminum application, and exclude nonstructural members from the equivalence/load-path assessment.
unresolved_decisions: Actual member sizes and application/material matrix TBD.

obligations.title: Meet all steel minima and prescribed calculation properties
obligations.statement: For each steel class satisfy all four simultaneous minima (inertia mm^4, area mm^2, outside diameter/square width mm, wall mm): A=(11320,173,25.0,2.0), B=(8509,114,25.0,1.2), C=(6695,91,25.0,1.2), D=(18015,126,35.0,1.2). Example round tubes are A:1.0 in x 0.095 in or 25 x 2.5 mm; B:1.0 in x 0.065 in or 25.4 x 1.6 mm; C:1.0 in x 0.049 in or 25.4 x 1.2 mm; D:1.375 in x 0.049 in or 35 x 1.2 mm. Examples are not additional compulsory sizes. For any steel in SES calculations use continuous/nonwelded E=200 GPa(29000 ksi), Sy=305 MPa(44.2 ksi), Su=365 MPa(52.9 ksi); for discontinuous/welded joint calculations use Sy=180 MPa(26 ksi), Su=300 MPa(43.5 ksi). If welded reinforcement is needed, prove equivalence of the welded tube plus reinforcement to the original nonwelded tube. Welded inserts have thicker walls and smaller outer diameter/square side than that original tube and are welded at both ends. Do not mechanically alter structural weld shapes.
conditions_and_alternatives: All four class minima apply together; weld and reinforcement conditions are not optional substitutes.
obligations.verification_obligation: Measure selected tubing and calculate inertia/area. Audit SES material cards, continuous/joint properties, reinforcement equivalence, insert dimensions and both end welds; inspect structural welds for mechanical reshaping.
unresolved_decisions: Steel grade, purchased dimensions/tolerances, members, joints and reinforcement details TBD.

obligations.title: Retain conditional aluminum construction and evidence
obligations.statement: Use aluminum tubing only in applications permitted by the application table. The SES includes material identity/properties with purchase, shipping or donation evidence, equivalence calculations against the steel minima/nonwelded reference in yield/ultimate bending, buckling, tension, buckling modulus and energy dissipation, plus manufacturing process details. Aluminum wall minima are 2.0 mm nonwelded and 3.0 mm welded. SES nonwelded 6061-T6 values are E=69 GPa(10000 ksi), Sy=240 MPa(34.8 ksi), Su=290 MPa(42.1 ksi); welded values Sy=115 MPa(16.7 ksi), Su=175 MPa(25.4 ksi). Use the alloy's as-welded equivalent yield strength unless detailed proof establishes correct solution treatment/artificial aging and absence of later manufacturing heating. Postweld strengthening evidence identifies the facility, process and fixturing.
conditions_and_alternatives: Only if aluminum is selected; no aluminum material or heat-treatment waiver is selected.
obligations.verification_obligation: Audit material provenance, thicknesses, manufacturing records, reference-property use and every equivalence mode. If claiming postweld strength recovery, review complete treatment/fixturing/thermal history evidence.
unresolved_decisions: Aluminum applicability, alloy, welding and heat-treatment choices TBD.

obligations.title: Provide hoops and restrained helmet clearances
obligations.statement: Provide front and main hoops triangulated into the primary structure by structural tubing. A hoop bend below its brace is triangulated at a side-view node or is strictly less than 25 mm from the applicable F.7.8 attachment. With the restraint installed, both the 95th-percentile male and every team driver's helmet have at least 50 mm clearance from the line joining hoop tops and, for rearward main bracing, at least 50 mm from the line from main-hoop top to brace lower end. With forward main bracing, the helmet lies no farther rearward than the main hoop's rear surface.
conditions_and_alternatives: Brace direction controls the helmet envelope; the alternative bend treatment must be explicitly selected.
obligations.verification_obligation: Inspect hoops and load-path triangulation, measure each bend/attachment and restrained helmet clearance for the anthropometric template and all team drivers in the selected bracing configuration.
unresolved_decisions: Hoop geometry, brace direction, bend nodes, attachment type and driver envelopes TBD.

obligations.title: Use the prescribed template and inspection position
obligations.statement: Represent hips/buttocks and shoulder/cervical regions by two 200 mm circles and helmeted head by a 300 mm circle, with tangent neck lines. Centers of the 200 mm circles are 490 mm apart; shoulder-to-head centers are 280 mm apart. Place the seat rearmost and pedals most forward; the lower-circle center is at least 915 mm from the pedals' rearmost face, the middle circle rests on the seat back and the head circle is no more than 25 mm from the head restraint in the driving helmet location.
conditions_and_alternatives: This inspection template does not replace the full required driver population.
obligations.verification_obligation: Construct and dimension-check the prescribed template. Record its placement with seat/pedal extremes and verify 915 mm minimum and 25 mm maximum gaps before evaluating helmet geometry.
unresolved_decisions: Seat/pedal adjustment ranges, head-restraint adjustment and physical template evidence TBD.

obligations.title: Constrain front-hoop material and geometry
obligations.statement: Use closed metal tubing of the prescribed class for a front hoop rising from the lowest frame member on one side to the lowest on the other. Multiple pieces require correct triangulation. Its top is at least as high as the steering-wheel top in every angular position. Its rear surface is at most 250 mm forward of the wheel rim's forwardmost surface, measured horizontally on centerline with steering straight. Above the upper side-impact structure, side-view inclination is strictly below 20 degrees from vertical. A nonsteel hoop has an accessible 4 mm inspection hole. Avoid concave top-perimeter sections as the source recommendation.
conditions_and_alternatives: Front hoop material remains unselected; the nonsteel inspection-hole condition is retained.
obligations.verification_obligation: Inspect class/material, multi-piece triangulation and lower endpoints; sweep wheel positions, measure centerline distance and hoop inclination, and inspect the conditional hole and recommended top profile.
unresolved_decisions: Front hoop material, tube shape and wheel/hoop layout TBD.

obligations.title: Provide the continuous steel main hoop and its bracing
obligations.statement: Make the main hoop one uncut continuous closed steel tube of class A, spanning the lowest frame members or monocoque bottom. Above the upper side-impact attachment its side-view inclination is strictly below 10 degrees from vertical; below it, forward inclination is unrestricted but rearward inclination is at most 10 degrees. At the bottom-major-structure attachments, front-view inside spacing is at least 380 mm. Provide left and right straight, unbent closed steel class B braces: forward when the hoop leans forward, rearward when it leans rearward, either direction if vertical. Attach no more than 160 mm below the hoop top, preferably as near its top as possible, at an included angle of at least 30 degrees. Securely integrate braces to carry all hoop loads to the major structure without failure.
conditions_and_alternatives: Mandatory steel applications cannot be replaced with the permitted aluminum alternatives for other members.
obligations.verification_obligation: Inspect continuous steel construction, class and brace count; measure angles, spacing and attachment height. Substantiate integration and full load transfer using the applicable chassis/bracing support and joint rules.
unresolved_decisions: Main hoop/brace geometry, joining method, support design and load evidence TBD.

obligations.title: Retain the tube-frame side-impact alternative
obligations.statement: For a tube-frame side-impact structure use closed tubing of the applicableB orD class, with at least three members on each side of the seated driver. Multiple pieces require straight unbent tubes and correct triangulation. The upper member joins the main and front hoops with its entire top edge in a ground-parallel 290–345 mm band above the lower member's lowest bottom point. The lower member joins both hoop bottoms. A diagonal ahead of the main hoop and behind the front hoop connects upper/lower members and completely triangulates their bays.
conditions_and_alternatives: Conditional tube-frame alternative; monocoque or hybrid choice remains unresolved.
obligations.verification_obligation: Inspect member count/class and straight multi-piece joints; measure the complete upper-edge band, hoop connections and bay triangulation for each side.
unresolved_decisions: Chassis construction, side-impact member sections, bends and nodes TBD.

obligations.title: Retain monocoque side-impact equivalence and physical tests
obligations.statement: For a monocoque define the side-impact zone between hoops as at least 290 mm of vertical height above the floor bottom plus half the horizontal floor. Establish equivalence to three class B steel tubes. The vertical portion from floor bottom to 345 mm above the floor's lowest bottom point is equivalent to at least two class B steel tubes and has no side-view openings between hoops. Calculate horizontal-floor equivalence under F.4.3. For a 25 mm-diameter laminate section show perimeter shear of at least 7.5 kN by the F.4.2.5 physical test and include results in the SES.
conditions_and_alternatives: Conditional monocoque alternative; no fabricated laminate strength is asserted.
obligations.verification_obligation: Review the selected side/floor geometry and F.4.3 equivalence calculations, inspect absence of vertical-side openings and obtain the specified laminate perimeter-shear test/SES records.
unresolved_decisions: Laminate/core geometry, equivalence data, coupons and SES evidence TBD.

obligations.title: Place the attenuator and AIP in a protected load path
obligations.statement: Locate the impact attenuator ahead of the front bulkhead with an anti-intrusion plate between them. Both attenuator-to-AIP and AIP-to-bulkhead attachments carry transverse and vertical loads from off-axis impacts.
conditions_and_alternatives: All attenuator/AIP construction and attachment variants.
obligations.verification_obligation: Review the physical stack and establish transverse/vertical load paths at both attachments under off-axis impact cases.
unresolved_decisions: Front bulkhead, AIP, attenuator and off-axis load-path design TBD.

obligations.title: Retain AIP material and attachment alternatives
obligations.statement: Choose a solid steel AIP at least 1.5 mm thick, solid aluminum at least 4.0 mm thick, or a composite meeting F.8.3. For welding, the profile reaches or exceeds the bulkhead tube centerline on every side; for bolting/bonding/laminating it reaches or exceeds the complete outer bulkhead periphery. Document direct attachment in SES. Weld lengths are at least 25 mm with interrupted weld/space ratio at least 1:1. Bolting uses at least eight critical fasteners at least 8 mm or 5/16 in diameter, with bolt centers at least 50 mm apart, and 15 kN pullout/bending capacity per attachment. Tearout is 15 kN per bolt or total mounting tearout exceeds the F.8.5.3.b attenuator attachment strength. Bonding requires no bulkhead openings, bonding over the AIP's entire surface and shear/peel strengths strictly above 120 kN. Laminating places the AIP ahead of the outer bulkhead skin, encloses it fully and provides shear capability strictly above 120 kN.
conditions_and_alternatives: Material and attachment alternatives are constraints awaiting a decision, not multiple simultaneously selected designs.
obligations.verification_obligation: Select material/attachment, measure the corresponding profile/thickness/fastener/weld geometry and substantiate conditional strength and SES documentation for the selected method. Record the rejected alternatives with rationale.
unresolved_decisions: AIP material, dimensions and attachment method TBD.

obligations.title: Retain composite AIP strength and allowed substantiation paths
obligations.statement: A composite AIP must survive frontal impact and withstand at least 120 kN static load distributed over the minimum 200 mm by 100 mm attenuator area. Verify either by physical testing attached to a representative intended chassis section with fixture equivalent to the baseline bulkhead or the first 50 mm of the chassis (data valid only one competition year), or by F.4.2.2/F.4.2.5 laminate tests with three-point-bending and perimeter-shear calculations.
conditions_and_alternatives: Only if composite AIP is selected.
obligations.verification_obligation: Select and substantiate one allowed proof route; check load area, representative fixture and one-year validity for physical tests, or the referenced laminate tests plus both required calculations.
unresolved_decisions: Composite AIP selection, laminate/test data and proof route TBD.

obligations.title: Retain standard/custom attenuator and bulkhead-support alternatives
obligations.statement: Select an approved event-site standard attenuator or design/test a custom one. A custom IA has fore/aft length at least 200 mm and height at least 100 mm by width at least 200 mm for at least 200 mm ahead of the bulkhead. Bond all segmented foam pieces against sliding/parallelogram distortion; place continuous panels between segments of multisegment honeycomb. If the bulkhead outside profile exceeds 400 mm by 350 mm or standard honeycomb is used, provide a full-opening diagonal/X support of class C or equivalent for monocoques, with each end carrying at least 30 kN in any direction, or perform F.8.8.6/.7 tests proving permanent AIP deflection is at most 25 mm.
conditions_and_alternatives: Standard/custom, foam/honeycomb/other, bulkhead profile and support/test alternatives remain unresolved.
obligations.verification_obligation: Pin the event-site approval/specification if standard is chosen; otherwise inspect custom dimensions/segments and obtain applicable tests. Evaluate the bulkhead/honeycomb trigger and establish the selected support or physical-test alternative.
unresolved_decisions: Exact approved standard IA or custom construction, bulkhead size and additional support/test choice TBD.

obligations.title: Constrain attenuator attachment and position
obligations.statement: Document IA attachment in SES. Standard/custom foam or honeycomb attaches by bonding; custom other construction may bond, weld or bolt. Bonds satisfy F.5.5 and shear strength strictly exceeds every applicable threshold:95 kN for foam,38.5 kN for honeycomb, and the maximum compressive force for a custom IA. Bond all foam surface; only precrushed honeycomb area counts for bond equivalence. Welds may be continuous/interrupted; interrupted ratio is at least 1:1 and each length is strictly greater than 25 mm. Bolting directly to primary structure uses at least eight critical fasteners of at least 8 mm or 5/16 in diameter, center separation at least 50 mm and each attachment 15 kN pullout/tearout/bending. Bottom leading edge is at most 175 mm above the lower side-impact structure's lowest bottom point. A custom IA has an area at least 200 mm long and 200 mm wide intersecting a ground-parallel plane at or below that 175 mm limit. Center IA laterally; standard honeycomb orientation is 200 mm wide by 100 mm high; standard foam may be lateral or vertical.
conditions_and_alternatives: IA/AIP choices remain unresolved. Preserve the different inequalities: AIP weld length >=25 mm versus IA weld length >25 mm.
obligations.verification_obligation: For the chosen IA variant inspect the allowed attachment, strength/provenance, weld/bolt/bond details, low-mounted area and orientation; include the exact method in SES.
unresolved_decisions: Attenuator type, attachment strengths, mounting height and orientation TBD.

obligations.title: Prevent front intrusion and preserve pedal clearance
obligations.statement: Ahead of the AIP in front view permit only IA, fastener heads and lightweight bodywork/nosecones; rearward nuts are recommended. Front wing/mounts must move entirely aft of the AIP without contacting the front bulkhead in a frontal impact; their attachment locations aft of AIP are recommended and tabs extend at most 25 mm ahead of it. At every pedal travel/adjustment position maintain at least 25 mm clearance to the AIP rear face, all front-bulkhead structure and all noncrushable items in primary structure, including batteries/master cylinders/reservoirs.
conditions_and_alternatives: Optional wing/bodywork installations trigger their attachment/motion conditions; pedal adjustment sweep is mandatory.
obligations.verification_obligation: Inventory front-view objects, inspect tab protrusion and evaluate wing/mount crash movement if present. Sweep pedal adjustments/full travel and measure clearance to every protected structure/noncrushable object.
unresolved_decisions: Front packaging, aerodynamic devices, adjustment ranges and collision/motion evidence TBD.

obligations.title: Combine attenuator and other frontal-object forces
obligations.statement: The combined IA assembly force and force to crush/detach other objects ahead of AIP cannot exceed the F.8.8.2 peak deceleration; exclude light bodywork, light nosecones and outboard wheel assemblies. Use peak loads 95 kN for standard foam,60 kN for standard honeycomb or the measured peak for a tested IA. Demonstrate the total by testing IA and noncrushable objects together, or testing objects alone and adding the specified IA peak; alternatively calculate mounting failure from fastener shear, tearout and/or link buckling and add the corresponding IA peak.
conditions_and_alternatives: The applicable material-dependent peak must be selected after IA choice, not combined or universally substituted.
obligations.verification_obligation: Inventory included/excluded frontal objects and select an allowed test/calculation route. Check each failure mode and the correctly matched attenuator peak against the functional deceleration reference.
unresolved_decisions: Front objects/mount failures, IA peak, proof route and combined force evidence TBD.

obligations.title: Keep the functional impact reference separate from test criteria
obligations.statement: Include an IAD report in SES. At the rule's reference total vehicle mass 300 kg and impact speed 7.0 m/s, the IA functional requirement is average deceleration at most 20 g, peak at most 40 g and absorbed energy strictly above 7350 J. The source explicitly identifies these as functional requirements rather than test requirements. This does not assign a 300 kg design mass to the actual car.
conditions_and_alternatives: Reference impact conditions are preserved, while actual vehicle mass and the substantiation method remain separate design/evidence decisions.
obligations.verification_obligation: Review the IAD functional demonstration and its mass/speed/energy/deceleration derivation; assess test interpretation under the remaining F.8.8 clauses before claiming acceptance.
unresolved_decisions: Actual vehicle design mass, IA performance and complete IAD evidence TBD.

obligations.title: Plan the applicable impact report, fixture, conduct and analysis
obligations.statement: For standard IA, omit test-data submission but include all other section requirements, photos of the actual IA and evidence against its specification (supplier receipt/packing slip is allowed). Nonstandard IAD includes functional test data, energy/deceleration calculations, test schematic and photos annotated with pre/post heights; IA testing is valid only one competition year. During tests use intended IA-to-AIP attachment and a representative chassis section/fixture equivalent in strength/stiffness to baseline bulkhead, not a solid bulkhead-shaped block. Leave at least 50 mm fixture clearance behind AIP; permanent deflection anywhere is at most 25 mm beyond its pretest position. Composite IA requires dynamic testing; other constructions may use dynamic or quasi-static. Dynamic tests occur at a dedicated facility under professional/faculty supervision, not a team-built dynamic apparatus; quasi-static tests may use university facilities with the source's due-care advice retained. Calculate average dynamic deceleration from raw unfiltered data. If peaks exceed 40 g, the permitted filter is CFC 60(100 Hz) underSAE J211 or a 100 Hz third-order low-pass Butterworth(-3dB at 100 Hz).
conditions_and_alternatives: Standard/custom and composite/noncomposite alternatives determine the evidence obligations; no test or approval is performed by model creation.
obligations.verification_obligation: Develop the applicable IAD package; review year validity, intended assembly and representative fixture, clearances/deflection, facility/supervision and test data. Reproduce average from raw data and document any allowed filtering of peaks.
unresolved_decisions: IA selection, dedicated facility, fixtures, current-year test data and official standard specification TBD.

obligations.title: Keep the official cockpit opening gauge path accessible
obligations.statement: Pass the exact page 56 cockpit-opening gauge horizontally/parallel to ground, inserted vertically from above intervening structure/bodywork between hoops, allowing fore/aft translation, until both at least 25 mm below the side-impact top's lowest point and at most 320 mm above the cockpit's lowest point. Gauge drawing dimensions are 600 mm overall fore/aft span, front transverse 400 mm, rear transverse 350 mm,100 mm rear bevel offset, and 75/100 mm top-profile offsets; use the actual official outline rather than treating those dimensions as a rectangular substitute. Wheel/column/seat/padding removal is permitted, but retain the firewall; retain shifter/shift/clutch unless integral with the removed wheel. Routing cannot obstruct the gauge. In practice the column remains and may be maneuvered around, never around fixed supports; an optional front-center column slot is allowed.
conditions_and_alternatives: Gauge outline and orientation are checked visually against the source drawing; T.1.2 internal cross-section remains outside this bounded interpretation.
obligations.verification_obligation: Construct the exact official gauge and document permitted/forbidden removals, unchanged firewall, routing and fixed supports. Demonstrate insertion to both limits without replacing the prescribed geometry.
unresolved_decisions: Cockpit opening/bodywork geometry, removable equipment and physical gauge demonstration TBD.

obligations.title: Contain the occupant and shield moving/sharp hazards
obligations.statement: Contain hips entirely within major chassis structure. With feet on pedals, feet/legs ahead of the front hoop stay inside/below structural tubing or equivalent in front/side views. Shield every moving suspension/steering part and sharp edge in the cockpit from the front hoop to a plane 100 mm behind pedals using solid material, including springs, dampers, rockers, antiroll bars, rack and column CV joints; make covers removable for mounting-point inspection. Protect the seat by keeping its lowest point at/above the upper surface of the lowest structural tube/equivalent in side view, or by a longitudinal class B side-impact tube below it.
conditions_and_alternatives: Seat protection alternatives remain unresolved; shields are functional hazards barriers, not permanent inspection obstructions.
obligations.verification_obligation: Check hips/feet/legs for all drivers and pedal settings, inspect the full hazard zone and removable shields, and measure the selected seat-protection alternative.
unresolved_decisions: Cockpit fit, hazard shields, seat and protection layout TBD.

obligations.title: Exclude track debris with a continuous floor closeout
obligations.statement: Provide a solid nonbrittle floor closeout from the feet to the firewall to keep track debris out; gaps between multiple panels are at most 3 mm.
conditions_and_alternatives: All vehicles; panel count and material remain unresolved.
obligations.verification_obligation: Inspect material, foot-to-firewall coverage and every panel gap; demonstrate debris exclusion and attachment integrity under the selected environment.
unresolved_decisions: Floor material, joints and attachment design TBD.

obligations.title: Isolate occupants and harness from fluids, batteries and TS
obligations.statement: Separate the driver compartment and every harness portion from fuel-system components if present, engine oil if present, liquid cooling and lithium batteries; for EV additionally separate all TS components except the specified outboard wheel motors and their cables at wheels/front arms. Extend the firewall so no body point less than 100 mm above the tallest driver's helmet bottom has direct sight to those hazards. Use a tightly mounted rigid nonflammable impermeable surface. For EV/lithium batteries, the battery/TS-side firewall layer is aluminum (not aluminum tape) and grounded per EV.7.7; the tractive battery container cannot serve as firewall. Seal the whole surface, edges, joints, passthroughs and floor against fluids; overlap/seal multi-panel joints, keep inter-firewall sealing unstressed, use passthrough grommets and environmentally rated sealants/adhesives.
conditions_and_alternatives: Human-driven EV baseline; conditional oil/fuel/cooling/lithium hazards must be inventoried, not silently declared absent.
Only the specific outboard-motor/cable exception is retained; it does not exempt the rest of TS.
obligations.verification_obligation: Inventory all hazards/harness paths and inspect sightlines for tallest driver, layers, ground path, container separation, mounts and complete seals/grommets. Substantiate material flammability/permeability and environmental ratings.
unresolved_decisions: Firewall geometry, aluminum layer/grounding, fluids/battery/cooling inventory and seals TBD.

obligations.title: Retain certified harness and posture-dependent alternatives
obligations.statement: Select a 5-,6- or 7-point harness certified to SFI 16.1, SFI 16.5 orFIA 8853/2016. Keep original labels/specification/expiration, use within the labeled expiration year (expiry on/before 31December of the competition calendar year is permitted), keep new/like-new condition without wear/cuts/chafing, follow manufacturer installation/threading and never modify supplied hardware. Five points are two lap/two shoulder/one antisubmarine belt; six use two lap/two shoulder/two leg or antisubmarine belts; seven add a negative-g/Z belt. Template seat-back angle at most 30 degrees is upright, strictly above 30 degrees is reclined; the chest-to-groin line follows shoulder belts to release buckle in side view. Reclined requires 6/7 points and either quick-adjust antisubmarine belts or two installed sets. All lap belts have tilt-lock quick adjusters; pull-up over pull-down is recommended. Use separate over-shoulder straps, neverY straps; H configuration is allowed.
conditions_and_alternatives: Posture, exact harness and certificate/specification remain unselected. Belt mount strength/angles are not claimed by this specification-only group.
obligations.verification_obligation: Select posture and harness, audit original manufacturer certification/expiration/condition/instructions/unmodified hardware, count belt paths and inspect required adjusters/strap geometry. Review all referenced mounting clauses separately.
unresolved_decisions: Driving posture, harness model, expiration, manufacturer documentation and mounting design TBD.

obligations.title: Provide and substantiate adjustable head restraint
obligations.statement: Limit rearward head movement with a vertical/near-vertical head restraint entirely inside the rollover envelope or permitted head-restraint protection. Do not attach other items to its material/structure or place items 25 mm or less away. Attach near top and bottom with strength at any load point strictly above 900 N rearward and 300 N lateral/vertical. For every driver, helmet rear gap is at most 25 mm and contact at least 50 mm from every edge. Approximate 100 mm longitudinal adjustment or multiple thicknesses is a source accommodation suggestion. Padding satisfiesSFI 45.2 or specified blue CONFOR CF45/CF45M underFIA List 17, is at least 38 mm thick and 15 cm wide, and has either area at least 235 cm^2 plus total height adjustment at least 17.5 cm or height at least 28 cm. Cover it with thin flexible material and an approximately 20 mm inspection hole on a nonfront surface.
conditions_and_alternatives: All drivers; material/area-adjustment versus fixed-height alternative and protection-envelope choice remain unresolved.
obligations.verification_obligation: Inspect approved padding/cover/hole, containment and item exclusion; measure fit for all drivers and the selected geometry alternative. Substantiate mounts under loads applied anywhere with the strict strength inequalities.
unresolved_decisions: Head-restraint material, geometry/adjustment, mounts, proof loads and envelope alternative TBD.

obligations.title: Pad all helmet-contactable chassis members
obligations.statement: Cover every roll bar, brace or chassis portion a driver's helmet could touch with at least 12 mm padding meetingSFI 45.1 orFIA 8857-2001.
conditions_and_alternatives: Contact envelope for all required drivers and operating/incident attitudes; uncontactable areas need a substantiated exclusion.
obligations.verification_obligation: Sweep helmet contact envelopes and inspect complete padding coverage, thickness and material specification.
unresolved_decisions: Helmet envelope, padding selection and coverage evidence TBD.

obligations.title: Maintain hydraulic stopping under a circuit failure
obligations.statement: Provide brakes on all four wheels operated by a single control and able to lock all four. Use two independent hydraulic circuits; leakage/failure at any point leaves effective braking on at least two wheels. Each circuit has a separate fluid reserve via separate reservoirs or an OEM-style reservoir. A single brake on a limited-slip differential is permitted, not selected. Prohibit brake-by-wire and unarmored plastic lines. Use scatter shielding against drivetrain failure and minor collisions. Sprung brake components in side view do not project below the chassis lower surface. Treat every brake-system fastener as critical under T.8.2.
conditions_and_alternatives: Circuit wheel assignment and differential versus wheel-brake hardware remain unresolved; a common electronics/regen path cannot replace hydraulic braking.
Separate reserves in an OEM-style housing do not waive hydraulic circuit independence.
obligations.verification_obligation: Inspect single mechanical control, hydraulic separation/reserves/materials, critical fasteners, shielding and sprung packaging. Demonstrate four-wheel lock and inject every credible leak/failure to prove effective braking on at least two wheels.
unresolved_decisions: Circuit split, reservoirs, cylinders/calipers/differential, lines, shields, fasteners and performance evidence TBD.

obligations.title: Protect mechanical pedal strength and operation
obligations.statement: Pedal material/manufacture is fabricated steel/aluminum or machined steel/aluminum/titanium. Pedal and associated parts withstand at least 2000 N without failure of brakes, box, chassis mount or adjustment. The source explicitly says this is not a design criterion and allows seated-official maximum-force pedal testing; a 2000 N calculation alone is not accepted as completed design verification. Failure of non-loadbearing brake/box parts must never obstruct pedal or brake operation.
conditions_and_alternatives: Material and fabrication route are coupled alternatives; fabricated titanium is not an allowed listed option.
obligations.verification_obligation: Review selected material/process, load path and hazards from non-loadbearing failures. Substantiate the minimum strength and inspection pedal-test conditions with documented test/analysis evidence, not an invented universal design margin.
unresolved_decisions: Pedal fabrication/material, box/mount/adjustment, human force envelope and proof evidence TBD.

obligations.title: Keep regenerative braking optional and hydraulic actuation direct
obligations.statement: For this EV the first 90 percent of pedal travel may regenerate without hydraulic actuation; it is an option. The remaining travel directly operates hydraulics, and regeneration may remain active. No 90 percent deadband or regeneration strategy is selected until the complete brake/powertrain design is reviewed.
conditions_and_alternatives: If regeneration is used, coordinate the low-speed inhibition and brake/accelerator plausibility in the separately owned driver-demand slice.
obligations.verification_obligation: Decide whether and how regen is used; sweep pedal travel and prove direct hydraulic actuation in the remaining range even with disabled/failed regeneration. Review the referenced EV regenerative braking and conflict safeguards.
unresolved_decisions: Regen adoption, pedal transition, hydraulic timing and cross-slice interface contract TBD.

obligations.title: Open and retain the direct overtravel shutdown contact
obligations.statement: Travel beyond the normal brake-pedal range operates BOTS. Use a mechanical SPST two-position push-pull, push-rotate or flip switch that holds OFF; OFF opens the EV shutdown circuit. The driver cannot reset it. Implement the circuit with analog components, excluding programmable logic/ECU/similar digital controllers. The model reuses the shutdown slice's physical BOTS contact rather than adding a parallel or duplicate contact.
conditions_and_alternatives: Human-driven EV: EV.8.2.2 applies; the published IC reference is retained as nonapplicable to this electric baseline.
obligations.verification_obligation: Force brake overtravel, inspect mechanical SPST/contact holding and analog/direct wiring, prove the installed series shutdown opens and verify no seated/restrained driver can reset the contact.
unresolved_decisions: Overtravel threshold, normal travel/adjustment limits, switch rating/location and reset-access geometry TBD.

obligations.title: Signal braking with the required rear visibility and geometry
obligations.statement: Provide a rear brake lamp plainly visible in very bright sunlight. It is red on black, rectangular/triangular/near-round with lit area at least 15 cm^2, vertically between wheel centerline and driver's shoulder and approximately on lateral centerline. Undiffused LEDs are at most 20 mm apart; a single LED line is at least 150 mm long. These alternatives do not override minimum lit area/visibility.
conditions_and_alternatives: Lamp shape, LED/diffuser technology, brightness and trigger circuit remain unresolved.
obligations.verification_obligation: Inspect color/background, shape/lit area and installation heights/centerline. Apply the conditional LED spacing/line-length checks and demonstrate visibility from rear in very bright sunlight with the chosen brake activation logic.
unresolved_decisions: Exact lamp, wiring/activation, diffuser/LED layout and sunlight visibility evidence TBD.

visual_checks.26: F.3.2 application and F.3.4 steel tables
visual_checks.66: brake pedal options, BOTS and lamp dimensions

exclusions: This is not full V/F/T, full vehicle safety or full event-rule coverage.
F.4 composite testing, other F.5 joints/braces, F.6/F.7 bulkheads/supports, T.1.2 cross-section, T.1.6 thermal protection and T.2.4–T.2.7 harness mounting remain dependent unmodeled work.
Driver-demand owns APPS/BSE/EV.4.7/BSPD; shutdown owns EV.8 and the shared BOTS physical series contact.
Event-site anthropometry, approved IA and specification/FAQ inputs require official pinning before a hardware choice.
